messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@acmepayments.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acmepayments.com
Date: 2026-03-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Spike in failed requests — need telemetry slice and IRP

Hi Tessa,

We observed a short-lived spike in 5xx responses routed through your hosted inference endpoint (redwood-prod-us1) between 2026-03-14T22:07Z and 2026-03-14T22:18Z. Our engineering team saw ~2.6k failed attempts to the /v1/generate route and we've temporarily throttled traffic while we investigate.

Can you please: 
- Confirm whether Redwood saw any correlated errors or throttling events for our tenant (acme-prod) during this window.
- Provide a telemetry slice (logs + traces) covering 2026-03-14T21:50Z -> 2026-03-14T22:30Z, including request IDs, model variant, and node IDs.
- Share the incident response plan (IRP) contact and any SOC 2 relevant artifacts that map to detection/response controls while we triage.

We need this for our audit and to decide if we escalate to our risk board. Please treat this as high priority.

Thanks,
Maria Garcia
Sr. Site Reliability Engineer | Acme Payments

2) Marissa will assemble SOC 2 mapping for detection and incident response controls (CC6 / CC7 equivalent) and provide the IRP contact/roster for on-call.

Subject: Re: Spike in failed requests — telemetry slice attached

Hi Maria,

I've pulled the per-request traces and the scheduling logs for the time range requested. The initial signal looks like a transient overload on a subset of nodes running a large-sequence workload; the runtime retried a small fraction of requests which surfaced as 5xx to your client. Bundle includes request IDs, node IDs, model variant (rw-v2-13b), and system load.

Attached: acme_telemetry_slice_0315.zip (contains redwood-requests.csv, node-metrics.jsonl, span-traces.jsonl)
Transfer note: the zip is redacted for customer tokens (we removed prompt/response payloads) but preserves headers, timing, and error frames.

Next steps we suggest for your dev team:
- Temporarily reduce client-side max tokens for long prompts or use streaming fallback.
- We can provision a dedicated pool if steady long-sequence traffic is expected.

If you'd like us to run a replay against a staging variant and capture kv-cache pressure analytics we can do that; it'll require a short maintenance window.

-Karthik
Software Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference

Subject: Final update: redacted postmortem and evidence handoff

Maria — attaching the redacted postmortem and the confirmation of telemetry retention per our policy. Summary:
- Root cause: transient scheduler overload on a small subset of inference nodes processing long-sequence batched requests. No data exfiltration detected.
- Impact: ~0.3% of total requests for acme-prod during window returned 5xx; latency spikes observed for long prompts.
- Remediation: increased autoscaler buffer for long-sequence workloads, additional KV-cache tuning, and an ops playbook to divert long sequences to a staging variant when node saturation approaches threshold.

Attached: redacted_postmortem_draft.pdf (PII/token redacted), acme_telemetry_slice_0315.zip (retained for 90 days).

Per your SOC 2 ask: the attached mapping shows where these artifacts map to our detection and response controls. If the Acme audit team needs an attestation letter, please open HS-93214 and we'll produce a formal statement.

If you'd like a short postmortem review call for your risk board, I can set 30 minutes tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Incident Response Lead | Redwood Inference
